design:
Each weak visual was refined on the isolation bench first (`vision/isolation_v013.md`): the template forced alone into a picture, cut out with nothing else around it and read blind by a fresh reader, five rounds and 36 cut-outs in all. The first round found the pinched hose's bulge read as "a puddle, a hose connector or bulge, or a second shadow" and the hose rising to the hand "more like a pole"; the curled-up cat, turned so it would be large enough, as "stretched out on its belly ... collapsed, injured or dead"; the leaf sprays over the stuck kite as "spiky scribbles or starbursts"; and the raised box over the garden fence as "resting at a tilt on top of the hedge". The stalking cat with its lifted paw ("stalking or about to pounce on the bird"), the curled-up dog ("curled up in a compact ball with its head down ... sleeping"), the shorter pram handle, the heavier stand and the child inside the sandbox read as intended at once. The rest were redrawn and read again until they did: the hose "the dog standing on the hose and blocking the water, with pressure building up behind it", the cat, with a new shorter, rounder pose, "curled up ... asleep or resting", the kite "clumps of leaves are drawn on top of the kite ... which suggests it is caught in the tree", the box "in mid-air against a light blue sky". Two drawings of the kite were dropped on the way: leaves in the crown's own green with no edge left "a lopsided ... shape with a notch", and a kite hung from the crown's rim read as "flying just beside or behind the tree".

Then the changes were read blind in whole test scenes among other events, two rounds and ten pictures, one reader each, with the screen's own prompt (`vision/design_tests_v013.md`). The hose read as intended first in both of its pictures ("the bulge ends right where the dog's back paw is, so the dog seems to be standing on the hose and blocking the water"), the kite as stuck in all four, the stalking cat as stalking in all four. The scenes added five placement rules: no one lies or stands on the hose's run along the ground (a sleeping cat lay across it), sleepers keep open ground around them, the sleeping dog lies nearer the front (far back by the pond a puppy "looks asleep or sniffing"), the pram keeps clear of the market stall, and where there is a tree the gust strips a few leaves off it ("the trees ... show no sign of wind").
intro: The one template that failed in v0.12, `blocked_hose`, passed the tenth screen with full marks in all three of its pictures ("a white dog ... is standing right on the hose, and the hose is visibly swollen on the reel side of the dog, so the water is blocked"), and two of the three inferences that lost a half point there, the duck and the catch, reached full marks too. The sleeping cats and dogs read as asleep, curled up, in seven of their eight pictures, and the kite as "caught in the leaves" in all three. The set kept no item misread for the third time in four screens and scored 0.99 over all items; the gate passed 61 of 64 templates. The three that fail, `cat_stalks_bird`, `seesaw_heavy` and `wave`, each lost one or two half points in a single picture (`vision/flaws_v013.md`).
screen: Across all 61 pictures only 8 of 717 scored items fell short of full marks (8 of 694 in v0.12), every one a half point: a reading offered as one of two (a paw-lifted cat "may be chasing the red bird or just running past the girl"; a boy's raised hand "either waving or listening to something") or the visible facts given without the meaning (a girl up on the seesaw beside the heavy reader, "nothing looks wrong there"; a balloon "floating away", never said to have been let go). Seven of the eight fall in the set, so its inferences dropped from 0.96 to 0.94 (four half points over 35 items). Unintended oddities rose from 1.5 to 2.1 per picture. Most are mild ("odd but possible"), and one scorer filed ages and drawing remarks that earlier scorers mostly left out. None of the v0.12 oddities came back as reported then: no shadow with nothing above it, no kicked ball heading for a child, no throw toward a cat, no leaves pasted on the kite, no collapsed pet. The real ones are on the v0.14 list: a girl at an empty seesaw's raised end "could look like she is standing on it", the square-wheeled bicycle still "stands upright by itself with no stand", and the gust still leaves washing on the line and people's hair unmoved.
redrawn: `blocked_hose` reads with full marks in all three of its pictures, and the duck ("swimming quickly towards the food") and the catch with full marks in all of theirs. The stalking cat read as "crouched low, creeping" in two pictures; in the busiest street, beside a passing girl, it read as "running/pouncing", and lost two half points there.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (49 in three, 13 in four, 2 in six). The three failures each lost one or two half points in one picture: the stalking cat in the busy street, the heavy seesaw where the girl's predicament went unremarked, and a small boy's wave read as "waving or listening". The retest of v0.9 put reader variance at about five templates between screens; 61 is within it of v0.12's 63.
